policy_extraction.penalties_summary: None specified in this Discussion Paper. The paper explicitly disclaims imposing binding monitoring expectations or immediate mandates, prioritizing voluntary industry efforts, agile governance, safe harbors, and ongoing supervisory dialogue—while reiterating that existing technology-neutral financial statutes (such as the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act and APPI) and supervisory guidelines remain enforceable regardless of AI use.
policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Version 1.1 (March 2026) of the Financial Services Agency's AI Discussion Paper, updating Ver. 1.0 with insights from the June–December 2025 FSA AI Public-Private Forum and reflecting Japan's May 2025 AI Promotion Act and December 2025 Basic AI Plan. Covers conventional AI, generative AI (internal, indirect customer, and direct customer deployments), and emerging AI agents / agentic AI across 130 surveyed financial institutions, detailing emerging customer-facing guardrails (Box 4), AI-agent lifecycle/permission platforms, APPI and FIEA regulatory clarifications, systemic financial-stability risks, regional-bank GenAI DX pilots (Box 5), and FSA's own SupTech AI initiatives.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The FSA AI Discussion Paper (Version 1.1) is dominantly framed around innovation enablement, warning against the 'risk of not taking on challenges', emphasizing agile governance and risk-based soft law over chilling mandates, offering safe harbors, regulatory-clarity desks, and PoC hubs, and encouraging active public-private dialogue so financial institutions can deploy generative AI and AI agents confidently. Consumer and public safety is a prominent secondary frame focused on protecting financial customers and market stability from hallucinations, deceptive solicitation, AI-enabled deepfake fraud and KYC evasion, cyberattacks, and systemic herding or disinformation-driven market instability. Economic competitiveness forms a substantive third frame—positioning Japanese financial innovation to lead globally, transform business models, strengthen regional economies via regional-bank DX, and realize an international financial center—paired with fundamental rights (safeguarding personal data under APPI, mitigating structural algorithmic discrimination in credit and HR, and ensuring explainability) and a notable labor and workforce transition thread addressing labor shortages, employee job-displacement anxiety, and workforce reskilling.

evidence_spans.quote: 金融機関等においては、個人情報保護に係る適切な対応と個人情報を含むデータの効果的な活用の両立が求められており、金融庁としても、継続的な対話を通じて金融機関の取組みの把握を行っていく。
evidence_spans.quote_en: Financial institutions are required to balance appropriate personal-information protection with effective utilization of data including personal information, and the FSA will continue monitoring institutions' efforts through ongoing dialogue.

evidence_spans.quote: 加えて、AI に対する個々人の理解度に差があることや、自分の業務がAI に代替されるのではないかとの不安感から、ユースケースのアイデア出しや部門横断的な協力体制を構築しづらいとの声も多い。
evidence_spans.source_section: IV.1.①.iv 専門人材の確保・育成及び社内教育
evidence_spans.quote_en: In addition, many voices note that disparities in individual AI comprehension and anxiety that one's own job may be replaced by AI make it difficult to generate use-case ideas and build cross-departmental collaboration.

evidence_spans.quote: AI の導入が進む中で、金融機関等に求められる人材も大きく変容していく可能性があり、重要な経営課題の一つと認識して人材育成や社内教育に取り組んでいくことが期待される。
evidence_spans.source_section: IV.1.①.iv 専門人材の確保・育成及び社内教育
evidence_spans.quote_en: As AI adoption progresses, the talent required at financial institutions may also transform significantly, and institutions are expected to recognize talent development and internal education as a key management priority.
